description: Historical Sea Ice Atlas is a web tool or resource listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by Alaska Ocean Observing System; Alaska Center for Climate Assessment & Policy; University of Alaska Fairbanks | International Arctic Research Center | Scenarios Network for Alaska + Arctic Planning. View maps of historical sea ice concentration in the oceans surrounding Alaska from the mid-1800s through today. The atlas gives users the opportunity to view sea ice data from multiple sources in a single interactive map. Use this atlas to visualize how sea ice concentration around Alaska has changed over time in animations or images. Coverage: the United States, or as stated on the tool page. The toolkit lists hazards: Changing Seasons, Erosion and Shoreline Recession, Shifting Species, Habitats, and Ecosystems. Assets: Aquatic and Marine Resources, Natural Areas and Wildlife, Transportation and Mobility. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the tool itself was not opened or run, its licence and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support climate-adaptation planning and exposure screening. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
